slides.texte_overlay:
How To Never Run Out
Of Things To Say
Talk about the last thing that made you laugh. A video, a friend's mistake, a strange sign. Funny little stories are the easiest way to restart any chat.
Ask for their opinion on something small. "Best pizza place around here?" People love giving recommendations, and it always leads somewhere.
Keep three stories ready. A travel mishap, a childhood memory, something weird from work. Having them in your pocket means you're never stuck.
Notice the environment. The music, the decoration, the crowd. "This place used to be a bank, right?" What's around you is always a topic.
Fill your head with fun facts. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and one strange fact can carry a conversation for minutes.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. One strange fact can carry a conversation for minutes.

slides.texte_overlay: Go back to an earlier topic. "Wait, tell me more about that trip." Returning to something they mentioned shows you were really listening.
Share what you're excited about. A project, a trip, a new hobby. Enthusiasm is contagious, and people open up when you do. Energy invites energy.
